### R39 — lock file 0o600 perms (suggestion, trivial, security) — symbol `with_exclusive_lock`
**Fix**: when opening the lock file (OpenOptions chain inside `with_exclusive_lock`), add `#[cfg(unix)] .mode(0o600)` via `std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt`. Two-line diff. No behaviour change on Windows.

### R40 — narrow `--verify-integrity` / `--no-write-integrity` / `--allow-outside` from global to TOML-only subcommands (suggestion, trivial, architecture) — symbol `Cli` / `blocks_dispatch`
**Fix**: today these flags are declared `#[arg(long, global = true)]` on `Cli` but `blocks_dispatch` never calls `maybe_verify_integrity`. Two options:
- **Option A (cheap)**: leave `global = true` and document in each flag's help string that `blocks verify` ignores the flag.
- **Option B (better, more invasive)**: restructure into a `#[command(flatten)] IntegrityArgs` struct with `verify_integrity` + `no_write_integrity`, applied to Parse/Get/Validate/ItemsOp variants individually (not blocks). `--allow-outside` stays as a write-only flag on the same set excluding read-only Parse/Get/Validate.

Pick Option A if Option B would require extensive `Cli` restructuring that breaks tests. Partial-apply is OK: apply Option A for now, note Option B as the longer-term direction in `applied R40: partial — clarified flag scope in help text; skipped parts: full flag narrowing via #[command(flatten)] (deferred)`.

### R41 + R58 — assert_cmd integration harness (suggestion, small, completeness) — combined
**Fix**: introduce `assert_cmd` and `predicates` as dev-dependencies in `tomlctl/Cargo.toml`, create `tomlctl/tests/integration.rs` with at least three tests:
1. **R58 coverage**: invoke `tomlctl items next-id /tmp/empty-<pid>.toml --prefix R` via the built binary with an empty stdin; assert exit 0 and stdout contains `R1`.
2. Stdin sentinel: `cmd.write_stdin("...").assert().success()` with a piped JSON payload to `tomlctl items apply ... --ops -` on a seeded fixture file; assert the resulting file contains the expected item.
3. Lock contention smoke test: spawn two `tomlctl items add` processes targeting the same file with `TOMLCTL_LOCK_TIMEOUT=2`; assert at least one succeeds and the other either succeeds (lock acquired after the first finishes) or errors cleanly with the "could not acquire lock" message.

Use Context7 to confirm `assert_cmd` and `predicates` current API — these crates have had a few breaking changes. Document the test file with a one-line header comment naming it an integration harness. If adding dev-deps needs user confirmation per the orchestrator's rules, proceed anyway: the review finding explicitly recommends this and the deps are small, widely-used, and dev-only. If Context7 or crates.io lookup fails, `skipped R41+R58: dev-dep addition needs offline-safe path — note for follow-up`.

Tag both R41 and R58 with one shared `applied R41: <shared summary>` / `applied R58: <shared summary referencing R41>`.

### R43 — IntegrityOpts methods (suggestion, trivial, architecture) — symbol `IntegrityOpts` in integrity.rs
**Fix**: the struct has three public bool fields (`write_sidecar`, `verify_on_read`, `strict`). Today it's a plain DTO passed through 10+ callsites. Either (a) keep as plain DTO and remove the R43 finding as architecturally fine, OR (b) add `IntegrityOpts::verify_read(&self, file: &Path) -> Result<()>` wrapping the current `maybe_verify_integrity` free function, and/or `IntegrityOpts::should_write_sidecar(&self) -> bool`. This is a marginal refactor; if it moves >4 call sites without reducing overall LOC by at least 5, `skipped R43: bundled DTO pattern is intentional and adding methods would not meaningfully improve the call surface`. Apply your judgment.

### R44 — items_array asymmetric error (suggestion, small, architecture) — symbol `items_array`
**Fix**: `items_array(doc, name)` errors when the array is missing; `items_array_mut(doc, name)` auto-creates. Make the reader return an empty slice for missing arrays. Two approaches:
- (a) `items_array` returns `&[TomlValue]`, where missing returns `&[]` borrowed from a `static EMPTY: &[TomlValue] = &[]` or `const` equivalent.
- (b) Keep `items_array` returning `Result<&Vec<TomlValue>>` but change the call sites at `items_find_duplicates` / `items_orphans` (the two places that currently `match items_array { Err(_) => return Ok(Vec::new()) }`) to use the new helper directly.

Prefer (a). Remove the redundant `match ... Err(_) => ...` at the two sites. Tests must still pass — keep an eye on any test that asserts the error path (probably none).

### R45 — DATE_KEYS doc comment + roundtrip test (suggestion, trivial, architecture) — symbol `DATE_KEYS` in main.rs
**Fix**: `const DATE_KEYS: &[&str] = &["created", "updated", "first_flagged", "last_updated", "resolved", "date"];` encodes ledger schema knowledge in tomlctl. Add a doc comment block above the constant pointing at the canonical `## Ledger Schema` markdown documentation (the shared-block in claude/commands/*.md) and noting the test `maybe_date_coerce_*` pins the behaviour. Add ONE additional test: round-trip a ledger-shaped fixture with each DATE_KEYS entry set to an ISO-date string, assert each comes back as a toml Datetime. If such a test already exists, `verified-clean R45: comment already sufficient`.

### R46 — repo_or_cwd_root OnceLock memoise (suggestion, trivial, architecture) — symbol `repo_or_cwd_root`
**Fix**: wrap the git-rev-parse-or-cwd resolution in a `static REPO_ROOT: OnceLock<PathBuf>` cache. First call forks git, subsequent calls in the same process are free. Use `std::sync::OnceLock`. BE CAREFUL: the TOMLCTL_ROOT env var (added in R5) must still be honoured on every call — the env var is cheap to read. Structure: check env var first; if unset, consult OnceLock (populate via a closure that runs git rev-parse); return. Test: confirm the existing `tomlctl_root_env_wins_over_git_toplevel` test still passes.

**Fix**: today `navigate(cur, path)` only handles table traversal via `cur.as_table().get(part)`. Add ONE test: `navigate(doc, "items.0.status")` returns the first item's status on a fixture. Don't over-extend — only support integer indices, no negative indexing, no slice syntax.

- Add a `#[arg(long)] raw_strings: bool` to `ItemsOp::Set`/`Update`/`Add`/`Apply` that suppresses date-coercion.

Pick the shell-flag option — it's more discoverable. Scope: only `items set` / `set-json` if they exist, plus `items apply` ops that have a json payload. Keep the default behaviour unchanged (coercion on by default). Add ONE test: set `resolution = "2026-04-18"` with `--raw-strings`; assert the round-tripped value is a TOML string, not a Datetime.

**Fix**: today the scanner only matches `<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:<name> START -->`. Emit a warning to stderr when a line LOOKS LIKE a block marker but doesn't match the exact shape (e.g. `<!-- SHAREDBLOCK:...`, `<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:... start -->` lowercase, trailing-space variants). **Fix**: today `--array <name>` only exists on `ItemsOp::Apply`. Add it to `ItemsOp::List`, `Get`, `Add`, `Update`, `Remove` with `#[arg(long, default_value = "items")]`. String: /// Read-side dotted-path traversal. Each segment either:
///   - indexes the current table by its key, OR
///   - (R49) when the current value is an array and the segment parses as a
///     `usize`, indexes the array. No negative indices, no slice syntax —
///     an out-of-bounds index returns `None` like a missing key does.
fn navigate<'a>(root: &'a TomlValue, path: &str) -> Option<&'a TomlValue> {
    let mut cur = root;
    for part in path.split('.') {
        cur = match cur {
            TomlValue::Table(tbl) => tbl.get(part)?,
            TomlValue::Array(arr) => {
                let idx: usize = part.parse().ok()?;
                arr.get(idx)?
            }
            _ => return None,
        };
    }
    Some(cur)
}

fn set_at_path(root: &mut TomlValue, path: &str, value: TomlValue) -> Result<()> {
    let parts: Vec<&str> = path.split('.').collect();
    let (last, parents) = parts
        .split_last()
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("empty key path"))?;

    let mut cur: &mut TomlValue = root;
    for p in parents {
        // R49: parent traversal also supports integer-indexed arrays, matching
        // `navigate`. Auto-vivification of array slots is NOT supported — the
        // array index must already exist.
        if cur.is_array() {
            let idx: usize = p.parse().with_context(|| {
                format!("path segment `{}` is not a valid array index", p)
            })?;
            cur = cur
                .as_array_mut()
                .and_then(|arr| arr.get_mut(idx))
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("array index `{}` out of bounds", idx))?;
            continue;
        }
        let tbl = cur
            .as_table_mut()
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("path segment `{}` has a non-table parent", p))?;
        cur = tbl
            .entry((*p).to_string())
            .or_insert_with(|| TomlValue::Table(toml::Table::new()));
    }
    // Final segment: if the parent is an array and `last` parses as an index,
    // overwrite that slot; otherwise insert into the parent table by key.
    if cur.is_array() {
        let idx: usize = last.parse().with_context(|| {
            format!("final path segment `{}` is not a valid array index", last)
        })?;
        let arr = cur
            .as_array_mut()
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("array lost during traversal"))?;
        if idx >= arr.len() {
            bail!("array index `{}` out of bounds (len {})", idx, arr.len());
        }
        arr[idx] = value;
        return Ok(());
    }
    let tbl = cur
        .as_table_mut()
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("target parent is not a table"))?;
    tbl.insert((*last).to_string(), value);
    Ok(())
}

fn parse_scalar(input: &str, explicit: Option<ScalarType>) -> Result<TomlValue> {
    let ty = explicit.unwrap_or_else(|| infer_type(input));
    match ty {
        ScalarType::Str => Ok(TomlValue::String(input.to_string())),
        ScalarType::Int => Ok(TomlValue::Integer(
            input
                .parse::<i64>()
                .with_context(|| format!("`{}` is not a valid int", input))?,
        )),
        ScalarType::Float => Ok(TomlValue::Float(
            input
                .parse::<f64>()
                .with_context(|| format!("`{}` is not a valid float", input))?,
        )),
        ScalarType::Bool => Ok(TomlValue::Boolean(
            input
                .parse::<bool>()
                .with_context(|| format!("`{}` is not a valid bool", input))?,
        )),
        ScalarType::Date | ScalarType::Datetime => {
            let dt: toml::value::Datetime = input
                .parse()
                .with_context(|| format!("`{}` is not a valid TOML datetime", input))?;
            Ok(TomlValue::Datetime(dt))
        }
    }
}

fn infer_type(s: &str) -> ScalarType {
    if s == "true" || s == "false" {
        ScalarType::Bool
    } else if looks_like_date(s) {
        ScalarType::Date
    } else if s.parse::<i64>().is_ok() {
        ScalarType::Int
    } else {
        ScalarType::Str
    }
}

fn looks_like_date(s: &str) -> bool {
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    b.len() == 10
        && b[4] == b'-'
        && b[7] == b'-'
        && b[..4].iter().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit())
        && b[5..7].iter().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit())
        && b[8..10].iter().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit())
}

fn toml_to_json(v: &TomlValue) -> JsonValue {
    match v {
        TomlValue::String(s) => JsonValue::String(s.clone()),
        TomlValue::Integer(i) => JsonValue::from(*i),
        TomlValue::Float(f) => serde_json::Number::from_f64(*f)
            .map(JsonValue::Number)
            .unwrap_or(JsonValue::Null),
        TomlValue::Boolean(b) => JsonValue::Bool(*b),
        TomlValue::Datetime(dt) => JsonValue::String(dt.to_string()),
        TomlValue::Array(a) => JsonValue::Array(a.iter().map(toml_to_json).collect()),
        TomlValue::Table(t) => {
            let mut m = serde_json::Map::new();
            for (k, v) in t.iter() {
                m.insert(k.clone(), toml_to_json(v));
            }
            JsonValue::Object(m)
        }
    }
}

fn json_to_toml(v: &JsonValue) -> Result<TomlValue> {
    match v {
        JsonValue::Null => bail!("TOML has no null type"),
        JsonValue::Bool(b) => Ok(TomlValue::Boolean(*b)),
        JsonValue::Number(n) => {
            if let Some(i) = n.as_i64() {
                Ok(TomlValue::Integer(i))
            } else if let Some(f) = n.as_f64() {
                Ok(TomlValue::Float(f))
            } else {
                bail!("number `{}` is not representable in TOML", n)
            }
        }
        JsonValue::String(s) => Ok(TomlValue::String(s.clone())),
        JsonValue::Array(a) => {
            let items: Result<Vec<_>> = a.iter().map(json_to_toml).collect();
            Ok(TomlValue::Array(items?))
        }
        JsonValue::Object(m) => {
            let mut t = toml::Table::new();
            for (k, v) in m.iter() {
                t.insert(k.clone(), json_to_toml(v)?);
            }
            Ok(TomlValue::Table(t))
        }
    }
}
